locator.text: Display 81.2, p. 81, in the proof of Lemma 7.4

evidence: paper: \pm r'\big|_{r = \pm K_b/S_*} \;\le\; \frac{-2 c_\lambda K_b + C\left(1 + K_b/S_* + K_b^{2}/S_*^{2}\right)}{S_*} \;<\; 0.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The two endpoints of the paper's chain are stated exactly: the expression whose sign is asserted is, term for term, ±(E₂₁ + (-2λ + E₂₂ - E₁₁)r - E₁₂r²) at r = ±K_b/S_*, with c_λ = lamMin, |E_{ab}| ≤ eps = C/S_*, and K_b/S_* = coneConstant lamMin C / S_*. The paper's "sufficiently large fixed K_b and all sufficiently large S_*" is made explicit: K_b = 4(C+1)/c_λ (coneConstant, GrowingMode.lean:208) and S_* ≥ 2K_b (hlarge). What differs is the middle member of the chain, which the Lean never displays: it is used only inside the proof of upper_edge_factor_negative (hlin, hquad, hrate at lines 77-83), and there the bound reached is eps(1+r)² - 2 lamMin r = (C(1 + 2K_b/S_* + K_b²/S_*²) - 2c_λ K_b)/S_*, with coefficient 2 on the middle term where the paper writes 1. The rewriting is the paper's own generic-constant convention — bounding |E₂₂ - E₁₁| ≤ 2C/S_* gives the 2, and replacing C by 2C turns the paper's expression into the Lean's, with the same conclusion < 0 for large K_b. Nothing weaker is proved.
